diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, we used Green's identity, Lemma~\ref{lem: exact double layer}, and the condition $\sum_{j \in [M]} A_j = 0$, with $u(z)$ in~\eqref{e:uRep}.

issues.failure_explanation: The step equates the exterior (Ω-side) flux of D[φ] across ∂D_j with an integral of ΔD[φ] over the interior D_j. This requires that ∂_ν D[φ] has no jump across ∂Ω (Lyapunov–Tauber type result), and that the normal-derivative trace exists for merely continuous φ. Neither is established anywhere in the paper (Lemma 2.5 only gives the jump of D[φ] itself), and the expression '∫_{D_j} ΔD[φ](z^+)' is not meaningful as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the flux of u across a smooth curve γ ⊂ Ω homologous to ∂D_j (allowed since u is harmonic in Ω): the flux of D[φ] across γ vanishes because ∫_γ ∂_{ν_z}G(z−ξ)|dz| is constant in ξ on each side of γ (Lemma 2.4), while the G-terms give A_j by Lemma 2.4 and ΣA_k=0.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretive claim 'A_j can be interpreted as the flux across ∂D_j' in Theorem 1.2 is unsupported; the existence/uniqueness part of the theorem is unaffected.
issues.title: Flux identity in Theorem 1.2 assumes continuity of the normal derivative of the double-layer potential across the boundary without proof
issues.why_classification: A short standard replacement argument recovers the claim exactly; no result or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Since ϑ_1(z)=ϑ_1'(0)z+O(z^3), one has −(1/2π)log|ϑ_1(z)| = −(1/2π)log|z| − (1/2π)log|ϑ_1'(0)| + O(z^2), so c = −log|ϑ_1'(0)|/(2π). The appendix derivation itself yields log|σ̂| = log|ϑ_1| − πIm(z)^2/b + c̃ with c̃ = −log|ϑ_1'(0)|, which gives c = c̃/(2π) < 0, contradicting the stated positive sign. The Steklov appendix limit of S_2^k (with −(1/2π)log|ϑ_1'(0)|) is consistent with the negative sign and inconsistent with e:SigmaHat and (e: green approx).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace c by −log|ϑ_1'(0)|/(2π) in e:SigmaHat, in the expansion in Section 2 and in (e: green approx).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed representation (e:SigmaHat) and the local expansion (e: green approx) state an incorrect constant; no proof uses the value of c beyond its being a constant, so downstream results are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong sign of the constant c in the sigma-function representation and local expansion of G
issues.why_classification: A forced sign correction with no dependent reasoning; all claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: With ν(ξ) = −iξ'/|ξ'| one has ∂_{ν_ξ}G(z−ξ)|dξ| = Re[(1/2πi)(ζ−η_1(z−ξ)) dξ] + (Im(z−ξ)/b)Re[dξ], i.e. the complex line element dξ is required (as the proof's intermediate line correctly shows). With |dξ| as in the definition, the real part of the first integral is (1/2π)∫Im[ζ−η_1(z−ξ)]φ|dξ|, which is not D[φ]; so Lemma 2.9(1) 'Re f_D[φ]=D[φ]' and the periodicity constants in (1), and the Plemelj jump in (2), are false for the object actually defined in (eqn: complex double layer). The proofs of Lemma 2.5(4), Lemma 3.2(2) and their claims use f_D with these properties.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |dξ| by dξ in the first integral of (eqn: complex double layer), in (e:cauchy int) and in the final formula of the proof of Lemma 2.9(1); the proofs then go through as written.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 2.9 as stated is false for the defined f_D; the arguments in Lemma 2.5(4)–(5) and Lemma 3.2 that rely on Re f_D = D[φ] and the jump relation are formally unsupported until the definition is corrected.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential defined with arc-length measure |dξ|, making Re f_D ≠ D[φ]
issues.why_classification: The reasoning depends on the corrected meaning, but the fix is local and forced by the proof's own computation; all results survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The result directly follows from the Sokhotski-Plemelj formula \cite[Thm. 7.8]{kress1989linear}.

issues.failure_explanation: The Sokhotski–Plemelj formula (Kress Thm 7.8) requires Hölder-continuous density; for merely continuous φ the boundary limits of the Cauchy integral (equivalently of Im f_D, the conjugate of the double-layer potential) need not exist, and the principal value f_D[φ](z_0) need not be defined. The lemma is stated for all φ ∈ C(∂Ω), which the cited result does not support. The uses in Lemma 2.5(4), Lemma 3.2(2) and the tangential-derivative/Green's-formula steps of Lemma 3.2's Claim additionally need C^1 regularity of f_D up to ∂Ω, which is not established.

failure_location.quote:
\item  For $\phi \in C(\partial \Omega)$ and each $z_0 \in \partial \Omega$,
    \[
    f_\mathcal{D}[\phi](z_0^{\pm}) = f_\mathcal{D}[\phi](z_0) \mp \onehalf\phi(z_0),
    \]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Lemma 2.9(2) for Hölder-continuous φ, and note that elements of N(D−½I) and N(D+X−½I) are Hölder (indeed C^{1,α}) since φ = 2(D+X)φ with D: C→C^{0,α}→C^{1,α} for C^2 boundaries (Kress Ch. 7), which also supplies the boundary regularity needed in Lemma 3.2's Claim.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 2.9(2) is unsupported in the stated generality; the null-space characterizations in Lemma 2.5(4)–(5) and the injectivity in Lemma 3.2(2) rest on applying it to null-space elements without checking their regularity.
issues.title: Sokhotski–Plemelj jump for f_D claimed for all continuous densities
issues.why_classification: A standard hypothesis restriction plus a routine regularity bootstrap (citable) preserves every conclusion and use.

issues.failure_explanation: The continuous right-hand side is σS_0[φ] = σ(S(I−M)φ + Mφ). The discrete formulation drops the +Mφ term. Then both sides annihilate constant vectors, so det((D_s+½I)(I−M) − σS(I−M)) ≡ 0 for all σ (singular pencil; eig returns indeterminate eigenvalues), and for zero-mean χ=(I−M)φ the equation (D_s+½I)χ = σSχ imposes N conditions on an (N−1)-dimensional space, over-constraining the non-constant modes by forcing the free constant φ̄ to zero. Hence the written discrete problem is not a Nyström discretization of (e: steklov bie).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the right-hand side σ(S(I−M)+M)φ⃗, matching S_0; the constant vectors then give σ=0 and the pencil is regular.
issues.overall_effect: The Steklov algorithm as described in Appendix B is ill-posed and would not reproduce the reported eigenvalues (e.g. the correctly recovered σ_1≈0); the continuous Theorem 1.4 is unaffected.
issues.title: Discrete Steklov eigenproblem omits the mean term, producing a singular pencil that does not discretize (e: steklov bie)
issues.why_classification: A local, forced correction of the discretized operator restores the intended algorithm without loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: h^k_j = w^k_j \left| \frac{d z^{k}(s^k_j)}{ds} \right|$ for weights $w^k_j$ satisfying $\sum_{j \in [N_k]}w^k_j = 2\pi$

issues.failure_explanation: R_j^k(s) are already quadrature weights for ∫_0^{2π} log(4sin^2((s−t)/2))φ(t)dt (they contain the factor 4π/N_k = 2·(2π/N_k)). The single-layer integral is ∫_0^{2π} S_1^k(s,t)φ(z^k(t))|z^{k′}(t)|dt, so the correct entries are −(1/4π)|z^{k′}(s_j)|R_j^k(s_i). Multiplying by h_j^k = (2π/N_k)|z^{k′}(s_j)| introduces an extra factor 2π/N_k in the singular part of S, so the described matrix does not approximate S and the resulting eigenvalues would be wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace h_j^k by |dz^k(s_j^k)/ds| in the entries of S_1^k (or equivalently drop the 2π/N_k factor).
issues.overall_effect: The Steklov discretization as written in Appendix B mis-scales the logarithmic part of the single-layer matrix; the continuous theory and (presumably) the actual code are unaffected, but the documented algorithm is incorrect.
issues.title: Quadrature weights double-counted in the singular block S_1^k
issues.why_classification: A single forced scaling correction; no theoretical result depends on it.
